BETWEEN:-
 RAM SINGH GAMAD S/O LATE SHRI SAKARIYA GAMAD  @ CHATRIYA, AGE 63 YEARS, OCCUPATION: RETIRED  GOVERNMENT SERVANT R/O HOUSE NO 98-A  AYODHYAPURI COLONY KODARIYA MHOW, DISTRICT  INDORE (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (SHRI VIJAY KUMAR JHA- ADVOCATE FOR APPLICANT)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION CHANDERI DISTRICT ASHOK NAGAR  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (SHRI ROHIT SHRIVASTAVA- PANEL LAWYER FOR RESPONDENT-  STATE)
 This application coming on for hearing this day, the co  following:
 ORDER Affidavit of son of applicant filed in shape of Document No. 3727 of 2027 is taken on record.

This first application has been filed by applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.305 of 2012 registered at Police Station Chanderi, District Ashok Nagar (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468,
408, 409 of IPC.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant is in judicial custody since 20-04-2024 (as per arrest memo).

As per the case of prosecution, Chief Executive Officer of Janpad Panchayat Chanderi submitted a typed complaint to SHO, PS Chanderi District Ashok Nagar that local audit was conducted in the accounts of Janpad Panchayat Chanderi and the then Chief Executive Officer- R.S. 1 (applicant) was directed to deposit Rs.44,942/- along-with other Chief Executive Officers.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was suspected that concerned Chief Executive Officers have misappropriated the amount.
Therefore, the Commissioner (Panhayat) directed for lodging of FIR.

On such allegations, PS Chanderi registered FIR at Crime No.305 of 2012 for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 408, 409 of IPC against R.S. Gamad, P.S. Prajapati, Ramesh Singh Bhadauria and Ramesh Chandra Gupta.
Statements of witnesses were recorded.
Relevant seizures were made. Applicant- Ram Singh Gamad could not be traced and arrested.
Therefore, Final Report was submitted on 14-08-2024 in absence of the applicant.
The Trial Court issued permanent warrant of arrest to secure presence of applicant.
Applicant was arrested on 20-04-2024 in compliance with permanent warrant of arrest.
He is in custody ever since.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant was removed from service from 2007.
Thereafter, he was shifted to the house of his maternal grand father.
He was not aware of the prosecution, therefore, he could not appear.
Learned Counsel submits that the applicant is prosecuted merely on the basis of audit report.
No material was collected during investigation to substantiate charge of criminal misappropriation.
It is a case of irregularity in the accounting only.
The applicant is ready to deposit an amount of Rs.45,000/-.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
The applicant is aged around 60 years.
He has family to look after.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by applicant as the prosecution is based on documentary evidence.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and prays for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
